newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSIGHT - JGBs to continue demand-driven surge toward record.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - JGBs to continue demand-driven surge toward record.

text.p: Key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures are expected to make a try for an all-time high on Tuesday, receiving support from strong investor demand for cash JGBs, traders said.

"The 20-year JGBs to be offered through an auction will likely be well-received if the coupon rate is set at three percent. Also, traders who sold (JGBs) on Monday ahead of a series of straight bond launches may be forced to buy back," a trader for a city bank's securities unit said.
There is a good chance the June will rise above the record high of 127.30 set on LIFFE overnight, he said.
The market is concerned, however, that JGBs may have become overextended on the upside, traders said.
The fall of the benchmark 182nd JGB yield to less than 2.1 percent is causing market players to become cautious, a trader for another city bank's securities unit said.

The surge in JGBs has prevented market players from hedging their holdings of corporate bonds by selling JGBs, but once JGBs begin falling, players may place hedge sales of the bonds and this would accelerate the decline, the first trader said.
There has recently been a shift away from bank debentures and into JGBs, he added.
"Investment trusts and investment management companies have been selling bank debentures recently," he said.
They are pulling away from the purchase of bank debentures even though they have a need for instruments with four- to five-year maturities, he added.
Investors are selling bank debentures of all types and buying JGBs instead, he said.
The Finance Ministry is scheduled to make an offer for 20-year JGBs at 10.30 a.m. (0130 GMT). Traders said the coupon rate is likely to be set at 2.9 percent or 3.0 percent.
